Date: Tue, 23 Jul 2028 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Commitment ladder & fleet scaling sync

Team —

Following up for the weekly handoff: Finance asked for a concrete "commitment ladder" (tiers by $ and reserved GPU slots) that maps to the pipeline milestones for ACME's expected close windows. I attached a working workbook with our current ladder and a draft slot allocation by tier.

Ask: Can each of you comment on the cells below by EOD (Wed) so we have something we can route to Acme procurement for signature? Specifically:
- Laura: confirm pool sizing per tier (concurrent downstream jobs, expected qps).
- Karthik: flag any infra constraints or lead times if we need to pin capacity earlier.
- Ben: confirm commercial triggers and whether we can compress T+30->T+21 for tier-2 commits.
- Mina: quick check on finance approvals for the staged billing approach.

Attachments: [Attachment: commitment_ladder_v2.xlsx (Excel)]

Thanks,
Ava Chen
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ava_chen@redwood.com
[Attachment: commitment_ladder_v2.xlsx (Excel)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acme-corp.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Jul 2028 12:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Commitment ladder & fleet scaling sync

Ava / all —

Quick notes after a pass on the spreadsheet: I expanded the concurrent-job assumptions and suggested a small conservative buffer at tier-1 to avoid early throttling. Highlights:
- Tier 1: 8 reserved vGPU slots (baseline), target latency SLO retains <120ms for 8k tokens/session.
- Tier 2: 24 reserved slots with 30% burst pool; Karthik — this assumes 6–8 weeks lead time for additional racks if physical procurement is needed.
- Tier 3: 80+ reserved — recommend we model a mixed strategy: combination of reserved and burst credits across two regions to avoid single-region contention.

I attached the fleet playbook excerpt that maps these tiers to our autoscale and burst policies. If we lock Tier 2 earlier we can shorten lead time risk but it requires a stronger contractual commitment (see billing cadence tab).

On quoting Ava's asks: I can sign off on the pool sizing numbers today; Karthik, can you confirm the lead-time assumptions are accurate?

Laura Bennett
Head of Infrastructure Ops | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: fleet_scaling_playbook.pdf (PDF)]

Chiming in from the sales side —

Thanks Laura, that breakdown looks good and maps to our Q3 close windows. Two clarifications from commercial:
1) For Tier 2 compressing T+30 -> T+21 is feasible if we push a 10% higher upfront commit (revenue recognition and finance are aligned on that tradeoff).
2) For Tier 3 we should include a hard trigger clause at 50% pipeline coverage so we get an early notification to infra to pre-stage racks; operationally that reduces the 6–8 week risk.

Mina — can you confirm the staged billing language Laura referenced will keep Day 1 revenue recognition buckets intact? If so, I'll update the MOUs and loop procurement.

Appreciate the fast turnaround and the clarity in the tiers. A couple of asks from Acme procurement/ops:
- We have a hard deadline on availability for a pilot (week of Aug 28) — is Tier 2 timing compatible with that if we sign MOUs by Aug 4?
- For the pilot we'd like a 2-week burst credit to cover onboarding spikes instead of an immediate permanent reserve. Can Redwood provide that as a one-off?

If Tier 2 + 2-week burst credit is workable with the proposed compressed billing option Ben mentioned, we'll target Aug 4 for internal sign-off and submit PO the same day.
